title: Lubunga pupils’ march for school reopening during teachers’ strike
summary: Two local reports describe an actual pupils’ march in Lubunga on 7 Oct. MediaCongo Press estimates roughly one hundred pupils; 7sur7 says they called on government to address teachers’ claims. Approximate wording is retained; no exact lower/upper bound is invented.
attendance_reported: about one hundred pupils (approximate outlet wording)

occurrence.evidence: Both reports confirm the 7 Oct march; S005 gives about one hundred pupils.

date.evidence: Both body articles date it to 7 October 2024.

attendance_simultaneous.evidence: MediaCongo Press reports about one hundred pupils in the streets in a single march; approximate, not exact.

demand.evidence: S005 seeks reopening of schools and government intervention over teachers’ claims; S006 says pupils called on government to meet teachers’ claims.

notes: Approximate estimate is likely above the 50-person threshold but has no exact numeric bound. Source independence is not established; both are local contemporary accounts. No official response is described.
open_questions: Does any body-level source establish a precise simultaneous headcount or firmer lower bound than “about one hundred”?
Are the two accounts independent, and is any direct state response documented beyond the reported government-directed appeal?

title: Bukavu civic-society and market-committee march over municipal suspensions
location: Bukavu, South Kivu; march to provincial assembly and governorate
organizer: Civil society and Federation of Market Committees
summary: La Prunelle and Radio Maendeleo report an actual march on 9 Oct concerning municipal suspension of market committees and requests for governor/assembly action; no attendance count is given.

occurrence.evidence: Both bodies confirm a peaceful march on 9 October.

location.evidence: Bukavu; route included provincial assembly and governorate.

demand.evidence: Marchers sought reversal/review of municipal suspensions of market committees.

state_target.evidence: Municipal officials and provincial authorities were addressed.

notes: Two outlets’ relationship/origin is unknown; attendance remains unresolved. Officials received memoranda and discussed referral/review, but there is no documented implementation.
open_questions: Was a simultaneous crowd of at least 50 reported at the 9 October Bukavu march?
Are the La Prunelle and Radio Maendeleo accounts independent, and did the demanded official review lead to a later public action or response?

title: Machozi ya Raiya march in Uvira supporting teachers’ wage claims
summary: ACP reports an actual 7 Oct civic movement march supporting teacher pay and conditions; the deputy mayor received a memo to transmit it. Attendance is unreported.

occurrence.evidence: ACP reports a march held in Uvira on 7 Oct.

demand.evidence: Improved teacher living/working conditions and wages.

state_target.evidence: Memo received by deputy mayor for onward transmission; demand concerns public teachers and state pay.

notes: Distinct from the 9 Oct Uvira march; relationship within the broader teacher campaign remains uncertain. ACP body reports receipt/transmission of a memorandum, not policy accommodation.
open_questions: Was a simultaneous attendance of at least 50 established for the 7 October Uvira march?
Is this march part of the same teacher-pay episode as the distinct 9 October Uvira action, or only part of a broader campaign?

title: Uvira parents, teachers and pupils march over school closures and teacher commitments
location: Uvira, South Kivu; from Kavimvira toward the town hall
organizer: Teachers, pupils, parents, Nouvelle Société Civile Congolaise and intersyndicale
summary: La Prunelle confirms a separate 9 Oct march seeking resumed education and government honoring teacher-payment commitments; no attendance figure.

occurrence.evidence: Body reports an actual march on 9 October.

location.evidence: Uvira, route from Kavimvira toward town hall.

demand.evidence: Demanded that government honor teacher-payment commitments and education rights/resumption of classes.

state_target.evidence: Organizers explicitly asked the government to honor commitments.

notes: This is a different event from Machozi ya Raiya’s 7 Oct march. Shared teacher campaign is plausible, but no merge or continuity coding is automatic.
open_questions: Was a simultaneous attendance of at least 50 established for the 9 October Uvira march?
What evidence, if any, resolves its relationship to the 7 October march without merging separate dates?

title: Teachers’ multi-city march over a $500 monthly wage request
location: Several cities nationwide; Kinshasa participants were dispersed near Sendwe and Kasa-Vubu while heading to Palais du Peuple
organizer: Synergie des syndicats des enseignants de la RDC
summary: Radio Okapi reports teachers marched in several cities on 28 Oct; in Kinshasa demonstrators were dispersed and a delegation delivered a memorandum. No city-specific attendance is reported; no multi-city total is created.

occurrence.evidence: A peaceful multi-city march occurred on 28 October; Kinshasa route is stated.

location.evidence: Multiple cities; Kinshasa route toward People’s Palace.

demand.evidence: Monthly $500 salary and budget/payscale changes requested.

state_target.evidence: Teachers addressed parliament and government and delivered a memorandum.

attendance_simultaneous.evidence: No city-by-city count. Multiple-city participation is not aggregated.

notes: A different gathering from the 7 Oct Uvira/Kisangani marches and the 9 Oct Bukavu/Uvira actions. The article’s broad national formulation is not a national turnout total.
open_questions: What was the simultaneous attendance in Kinshasa or any other specifically named city on 28 October?
Are there independent city-level reports that document attendance without aggregating separate locations?
